about: The use cases page, as one noun: seven flagship ideas for what you can build from the same nouns and verbs, led by Tokens for Good, then a band of fields the same pieces fit. They are ideas, not results, so they carry no status, badges or evidence numbers. Each names the library packs that hold its nouns and verbs, by id; their titles come from site/content/library.json, and each links to its card on the library page. A flagship's rest finishes its name in a lighter type. scripts/build_site.py renders them into site/use-cases/index.html.
title: Use cases | ta-amps
description: Ideas for what you can build from the same nouns and verbs: tokens for good, videos made from code, feeds, shims, reusable code, continuous learning and long-horizon tasks.
heading: Use cases
lead: Each card is a use case: an idea for what you can build, not a result. The architecture underneath is the same for all of them, nouns and verbs, where verbs are tasks and nouns are everything a task uses or makes.

flagships.name: Tokens for Good
flagships.line: Spare tokens for good. It comes first because AI has to help everyone, not just the tech world. People donate AI capacity they won’t use, and nonprofits type what they need in plain words.
flagships.detail: Donated agents do the parts that public information can answer, with citations. Parts that touch private files become agent kits the nonprofit’s own agent runs.

flagships.name: Motion Graphics and Video Gen
flagships.line: Videos made from code, where every script, scene, voice line and caption is a noun and every step is a verb. Any agent can remake or extend a video, and every frame can be rebuilt from its source.

flagships.name: Feed Systems to Keep Your Agent Informed
flagships.line: Feeds watch repos, papers, releases and your own services. New items become nouns with their sources and follow-ups become verbs, so your agent knows what shipped yesterday. For example, server workers could track new memory systems and their benchmarks, so your agent can ask each week whether one fits its setup and is faster or cheaper.

flagships.name: Shimming Systems
flagships.line: A shim sits between any agent’s harness and its model. It adds the right nouns as context, or answers directly with no model call, without changing the agent.

flagships.name: Code Reusability
flagships.line: Tested code becomes nouns that agents find and compose instead of rewriting, and compiled recipes run with no model tokens.

flagships.name: Continuous Learning
flagships.line: Every finished verb leaves a result with a receipt. Learners turn those results into memory and routing advice, and small open models are tuned on checked examples, replacing the base only when they beat it on a test they never saw.

flagships.name: Long-Horizon Tasks
flagships.rest: via Atomic Steps and Decentralized Solutioning
flagships.line: Big jobs split into small, checkable verbs that many independent workers claim, attempt, review and finish, each leased and receipted, so nothing needs babysitting. Several workers can explore one brief through separate attempts.

fields.name: The same pieces fit almost any field
fields.line: Name the things your work reuses and the jobs it repeats, and any agent can pick them up.
